title: Relative Velocity Method
subtitle: Here you learn how to find the velocity of a point by relating it to another known point. This "relative velocity" idea is the engine behind all graphical mechanism analysis. Master this and acceleration problems become much easier too.
learningOutcome: Here you learn how to find the velocity of a point by relating it to another known point. This "relative velocity" idea is the engine behind all graphical mechanism analysis. Master this and acceleration problems become much easier too.

content.text: Here's the key idea: if you know the velocity of point A, you can find the velocity of point B by adding the velocity of B relative to A. It's like saying: "I know how fast the bus is going. To find how fast someone running on the bus is going, I add their running speed to the bus speed."
V_BA = velocity of B relative to A · V_A = absolute velocity of A · V_B = absolute velocity of B · ω_f = angular velocity of the link containing B · O₂B = length of that link
Angular velocity of a link (from velocity diagram)
V_BA = length of the relative velocity vector in the diagram · AB = length of the actual link

content.text: Common mistake — Not converting rev/min to rad/s before calculating. Always do: ω = 2πN/60. If N = 150 rpm → ω = 15.71 rad/s, NOT 150.
